# Risk memo: Defensive dividend

_Deterministic template memo. Verified: 0 unsupported numbers, 49 figures traced to code._

## Summary

Defensive dividend holds 6 positions (JNJ, PG, KO, PFE, XOM, WMT) and is compared with SPY. Between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29 it grew at 13.34% a year with annualized volatility of 14.68%, and its worst peak-to-trough loss was -28.29%. PG is 20.00% of the weight but 20.13% of the volatility.

## Return and risk profile

The Sharpe ratio is 0.73 and the Sortino ratio is 1.34, using a risk-free rate of 3.00%. The benchmark grew at 15.58% a year with volatility of 17.95% and a maximum drawdown of -33.72%. Beta to the benchmark is 0.52. The maximum drawdown ran from 2020-01-17 to 2020-03-23 and lasted 206 trading days in total. The effective number of independent risk bets is 5.71. Daily returns have skewness of -0.17 and excess kurtosis of 12.18; positive excess kurtosis means fatter tails than a normal distribution.

## Tail risk

On a typical bad day (1-day, 95% confidence, historical) the portfolio loses at least 1.26%, and the average loss on those days is 2.08%. At 99% confidence the historical VaR is 2.36% and the Expected Shortfall 3.85%, against a normal-distribution VaR of 2.15%. The 10-day 95% historical VaR is 3.27%. In a rolling backtest the 95% historical VaR was exceeded on 132 days against 113.2 expected (Kupiec verdict: consistent); at 99% the verdict is model underestimates risk. Over the next 252 trading days, a simulation assuming 5.00% annual drift gives a 36.73% chance of a loss, a median return of 4.20% and a 14.15% chance of a drawdown deeper than one fifth of value.

## Stress and regimes

Of 4 historical stress scenarios with enough history, the worst was COVID crash: the portfolio returned -27.30% against -33.72% for the benchmark. A regime model on the benchmark puts the market in a Calm regime (90.37% probability); in Stress regimes this portfolio's volatility is 5.5x its Calm level. In a walk-forward volatility test the best forecaster was GARCH-t, which forecasts annualized volatility of 17.56% for the next month.

## Disclosed risks from filings

- COCA COLA CO (KO) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([KO 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21344/000162828026010047/ko-20251231.htm))
- Walmart Inc. (WMT) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([WMT 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/104169/000010416926000055/wmt-20260131.htm))
- PFIZER INC (PFE) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([PFE 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/78003/000007800326000026/pfe-20251231.htm))
- Walmart Inc. (WMT) discloses a risk: Natural disasters, climate change, geopolitical events, catastrophic and other events could materially adversely affect our financial performance. ([WMT 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/104169/000010416926000055/wmt-20260131.htm))

## Caveats and limitations

- All figures are historical estimates from daily data between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29; future losses can be larger.
- Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall assume the past is representative of the future; the normal-distribution versions understate fat tails.
- Monte Carlo results depend on the assumed annual return of 5.00% and resample past daily returns.
- Regimes come from a hidden Markov model fitted to the benchmark; the current regime uses only data up to the last date.
- Disclosed risks summarize the latest 10-K risk factors; ETFs and funds have none.

_Educational tool, not investment advice. Models are simplifications; historical risk measures can understate future losses._
